name: St Alban's Church of England Primary School

areas.summary: Limited public evidence for curriculum (1 excerpt; mostly general statements rather than specific provision).

signals.text: The school must make it possible for th ose student s who achieve suitable grades at GCSE or equivalent to follow appropriate A level courses.

areas.narrativeSummary: The school must make it possible for th ose student s who achieve suitable grades at GCSE or equivalent to follow appropriate A level courses.

areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for enrichment and extra-curricular activity (5 specific items). Listed provision includes music, for example using music.

signals.text: We welcome the views of all those who participate in our worship, including pupils, parents, and visitors by the use of pupil and parent voice.

• CPD opportunities and sharing examples of good practice with other schools, such as St George The Martyr • Seeking to evaluate, formally and informally, with pupils and adults, activities with a particular focus on spirituality and spiritual development (e.g.

• Enable all pupils and adults to appreciate that Christians worship in different ways, for example using music, silence, story, prayer, reflection, as well as through the varied liturgical and other traditions of Anglican worship and festivals.
However, in view of the Christian ethos and distinctive Christian chara cter of our school, we hope that all pupils will participate in collective worship.
Class Mass: Each week a class participates is a class Mass in the church which they help to plan the music, prayers and readings.

areas.narrativeSummary: The school website lists music, for example using music. Information appears across 2 pages.

areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for ethos and values (28 specific items). Listed provision includes faith, worship, vision, pshe curriculum, respect, values, christian, resilience…. 6 items corroborated across multiple pages.

signals.text: It is an opportunity to bring the whole school community together daily to meet with God or connect with their own faith, to be still, to reflect on all that He gives us and to build our community up together in faith, hope and love.
Pupils should have a safe space to explore their own religious, spiritual and/or philosoph ical ways of seeing, living and thinking, believing and belongin g.

• Support for learning to live with success and failure for themselves and with others; school vision and it’s spiritual values, growth-mindset, Collective Worship, PSHE curriculum, Outward Bound residential.
• knowledge of, and respect for, different people’s faiths, feelings, and values • sense of enjoyment and fascination in learning about themselves, others, and the world around them.

As our spiritual nature is such a fundamental part of our humanity, spiritual development is a key part of this holistic view of education: “Our vision embraces the spiritual, physical, intellectual, emotional, moral and social development of children and young people.
